about: What a single shell command is and does: each program's base, the subcommands and options that change it, the wrappers that run another command, and the forms whose meaning the line cannot tell. A concrete command is its base with every modifier it carries; a chain is the union of its parts.

interpreted.note: code handed to an interpreter (python -c, node -e, a heredoc body, sh -c) cannot be judged from the table: a row marked interpreted is a write, and uncertain, only when its line carries the write check's content markers

unknown.note: a program not in the table: no write for the write gate, recorded so the next round adds it

(^|/)(tests?|suite)[\\w.-]*\\.(sh|py)$.label: testing
(^|/)(tests?|suite)[\\w.-]*\\.(sh|py)$.note: a script whose name says it runs the tests, run alone or handed to an interpreter

(^|/)(build|compile)[\\w.-]*\\.(sh|ps1|b.label: building
(^|/)(build|compile)[\\w.-]*\\.(sh|ps1|b.note: a script whose name says it builds

(^|/)(install|setup|bootstrap)[\\w.-]*\\.label: installing
(^|/)(install|setup|bootstrap)[\\w.-]*\\.note: a script whose name says it installs or sets up

-i.dialects: gawk -i inplace edits the file; other awks have no -i
-pi and -i.bak cluster the flag with others
-i.label: editing

-i.dialects: BSD sed takes a suffix word after -i, '' for none; GNU sed takes it attached, -i.bak
-i.label: editing
